question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Read the books of APJ Abdul Kalam, who was __a scholar. __
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"a man of letters"** refers to a scholar or a **literary person, **Someone who is** well-versed in literature and scholarly pursuits. **(साहित्यकार)​

 
 
• **Example: **Read the books of APJ Abdul Kalam, who was **a man of letters.**
 
 
 
• **​Scholar = **a specialist in a particular branch of study, especially the humanities.
 
 
• **Example **: "She was an eminent **scholar** in the field of Middle Eastern languages"
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment is **"a man of letters"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **a queer fish** (अजीब आदमी): A person who is strange or odd in their behavior.

 
 
• **Example:** John is considered** a queer fish** because of his unusual habits.
 
 
 
• **a dare devil** (निडर व्यक्ति): A person who is recklessly daring.
 
 
• **Example:** He is** a dare devil** who enjoys extreme sports.
 
 
 
• **a man of straw** (कमज़ोर व्यक्ति): A weak or insignificant person.
 
 
• **Example:** He was considered **a man of straw** in the boardroom.
